'''Sergei Kopeikin''' (born April 10, 1956) is a [[Soviet Union|USSR]]-born theoretical [[physicist]] and [[astronomer]] presently living and working in the [[United States]], where he holds the position of Professor of Physics at the [[University of Missouri]] in [[Columbia, Missouri]]. He specializes in the theoretical and experimental study of [[gravity]] and [[general relativity]]. He is also an expert in the field of the astronomical reference frames and time metrology. His general relativistic theory of the Post-Newtonian reference frames which he had worked out along with [[Victor A. Brumberg]], was adopted in 2000 by the [http://syrte.obspm.fr/IAU_resolutions/Resol-UAI.htm resolutions] of the [[International Astronomical Union]] as a standard for reduction of ground-based astronomical observation.

In September 2002, S. Kopeikin led a team which conducted a high-precision [[VLBI]] experiment to measure the fundamental [[speed of gravity]],<ref>{{cite journal|title=Testing the Relativistic Effect of the Propagation of Gravity by Very Long Baseline Interferometry |author= S. M. Kopeikin |doi=10.1086/322872 |volume=556 |issue=1 |journal=Astrophysical Journal Letters |pages=L1–L5|bibcode=2001ApJ...556L...1K|arxiv=gr-qc/0105060 |year= 2001 |s2cid= 2121856 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=The Measurement of the Light Deflection from Jupiter: Experimental Results |author= S. M. Kopeikin |doi=10.1086/378785 |volume=598 |issue=1 |journal=Astrophysical Journal |pages=704–711|bibcode=2003ApJ...598..704F|arxiv=astro-ph/0302294 |year= 2003 |s2cid= 14002701 }}</ref> thus, confirming the Einstein's prediction on the relativistic nature of  gravitational field and its finite speed of propagation.<ref>{{cite news |title=Einstein proved right on gravity |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/science/nature/2639043.stm|work=[[BBC News]] |date=January 8, 2003 |access-date=April 17, 2010 }}</ref>

He is also involved in studies concerning the capabilities of the [[Lunar Laser Ranging experiment|Lunar Laser Ranging]] (LLR) technique to measure dynamical features of the [[General Theory of Relativity]] in the lunar motion. He has critically analyzed the claims of other scientists concerning the possibility of LLR to measure the [[Gravitoelectromagnetism|gravitomagnetic interaction]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Physicist Says Testing Technique For Gravitomagnetic Field Is Ineffective |url=https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2007/06/070601104855.htm|work=[[Science Daily]] |date=June 2, 2007 |access-date=April 17, 2010 }}</ref> Kopeikin organized and chaired three international workshops on the advanced theory and model of the [[Lunar Laser Ranging experiment]]. The LLR workshops were held in the [[International Space Science Institute]] ([[Bern]], [[Switzerland]]) in 2010-2012.<ref>{{cite web|title=Theory and Model for the New Generation of the Lunar Laser Ranging Data|url=http://www.issibern.ch/teams/lunarlaser/|publisher=[[International Space Science Institute]]}}</ref>

Recently, S. Kopeikin has been actively involved in theoretical studies on relativistic geodesy and applications of [[atomic clock]]s for high-precision navigation and in [[geodetic datum]].<ref>{{cite journal|title=High Performance Clocks and Gravity Field Determination|author= J. Müller|author2= D. Dirkx|author3= S. M. Kopeikin |author4=G. Lion|author5=I.Panet|author6=P.N.A.M. Visser|doi=10.1007/s11214-017-0431-z |volume=214 |issue=1 |journal=Space Science Reviews|page= 5|bibcode=2018SSRv..214....5M|arxiv=1702.06761 |year= 2018|s2cid= 119335425}}</ref> He has provided an exact relativistic definition of [[geoid]],<ref>{{cite journal|title=Towards an exact relativistic theory of Earth's geoid undulation|author= S. M. Kopeikin|author2= E. M. Mazurova|author3= A. P. Karpik |doi=10.1016/j.physleta.2015.02.046|volume=379 |issue=26–27 |journal=Physics Letters A|pages= 1555–1562|bibcode=2015PhLA..379.1555K|arxiv=1411.4205|year= 2015}}</ref> and worked out the post-Newtonian concepts of the [[Maclaurin spheroid]]<ref>{{cite journal|title=Post-Newtonian reference ellipsoid for relativistic geodesy|author= S. M. Kopeikin|author2= W.-B. Han|author3= E. M. Mazurova |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.93.044069|volume=93 |issue=4 |journal=Physical Review D|article-number= 044069|bibcode=2016PhRvD..93d4069K|arxiv=1510.03131|year= 2016|s2cid= 119140663}}</ref> and [[normal gravity formula]].<ref>{{cite journal|title=Normal gravity field in relativistic geodesy|author= S. M. Kopeikin|author2= I. Y. Vlasov|author3= W.-B. Han |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.97.045020|volume=97 |issue=4 |journal=Physical Review D|article-number= 045020|bibcode=2018PhRvD..97d5020K|arxiv=1708.09456|year= 2018|s2cid= 119366302}}</ref> 
S. Kopeikin's workshop on spacetime metrology, clocks and relativistic geodesy is held in the [[International Space Science Institute]] ([[Bern]], [[Switzerland]]).<ref>{{cite web|title=Spacetime Metrology, Clocks and Relativistic Geodesy|url=http://www.issibern.ch/teams/spacetimemetrology/|publisher=[[International Space Science Institute]]}}</ref>

Kopeikin was born in [[Kashin (town)|Kashin]], a small town near [[Moscow]] in what was then the [[USSR]]. He graduated with excellence from Department of Astrophysics of [[Moscow State University]] in 1983 where he studied [[general relativity]] under [http://ufn.ru/ru/events/grishchuk.html Leonid Grishchuk]. In 1986, he obtained a [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in relativistic astrophysics from the [[Russian Space Research Institute|Space Research Institute]] in [[Moscow]]. His Ph.D. thesis was advised by [[Yakov Borisovich Zel'dovich]] and presented a first general-relativistic derivation of the conservative and radiation reaction forces in the [[Post-Newtonian expansion]] of the gravitational field of a binary system of two extended, massive bodies.  
In 1991, he obtained a [[Doctor of Science]] degree in Physics and Mathematics from [[Moscow State University]] and moved to [[Tokyo]] ([[Japan]]) in 1993 to teach astronomy in [[Hitotsubashi University]]. He was adjunct staff member in [[National Astronomical Observatory of Japan]] in 1993-1996 and a visiting professor in the same observatory in 1996-1997. Kopeikin moved to [[Germany]] in 1997 and worked in the Institute for Theoretical Physics of [[Friedrich Schiller University of Jena]] and in [[Max Planck Institute for Radio Astronomy]] until 1999. He had joined Department of Physics and Astronomy of the [[University of Missouri]] in February 2000 where he got tenure in 2004.

He has been married to Zoia Kopeikina (daughter of [[Solomon Borisovich Pikelner]]) since 1980, they have four daughters, four granddaughters and three grandsons. As of December 2019 the family lives in [[Columbia, Missouri|Columbia]], [[Missouri]], [[Texas]], [[Colorado]] and [[Minnesota]].

== Bibliometric information ==

Kopeikin has published 207 scientific papers and 2 books. He was an editor of two other books on advances in relativistic celestial mechanics. According to [https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=ATqskhQAAAAJ&hl=en Google Scholar Citations] program, the [[h-index]] of S.M. Kopeikin is 43, his [[i10-index]] is 101, while the total number of citations is 6552.
